title: Reviewing number and financial mathematics
summary: Integers, rounding, fractions, ratios, percentages, profit, income, tax, and simple and compound interest, with a worked example for each.

cards.title: Integer operations
cards.rule: Multiply or divide: same signs give +, different signs give −.

cards.title: Decimal places and significant figures
cards.rule: Look at the next digit. 5 or more rounds up; 4 or less stays.
lines: 0.04082 to 2 s.f. is **0.041** (start at the first non-zero digit)

cards.title: Rational numbers
cards.rule: Rational means it can be written as a fraction \(\tfrac{a}{b}\).
cards.note: \(\sqrt2\) and \(\pi\) are irrational: their decimals never end or repeat.

cards.title: Operations with fractions
cards.rule: Add or subtract: common denominator first. Divide: flip the second fraction and multiply.

cards.title: Ratios, rates and best buys
cards.rule: Simplify a ratio by dividing both parts by the HCF. A rate compares different units.
lines: $240 in the ratio 5 : 3: 8 parts, 1 part = $30, so **$150** and **$90**
Best buy: 500 g for $3.60 is **$0.72** per 100 g; 750 g for $5.10 is **$0.68** per 100 g, so the 750 g pack is better value

cards.title: Percentages and money
cards.rule: Per cent means "out of 100". Divide by 100 to get a decimal.
lines: Find the whole: 30% of an amount is $45, so the amount is \(45 \div 0.3 = \$150\)
cards.tip: check by working backwards: 30% of $150 is $45 ✓

cards.title: Percentage increase and decrease
cards.rule: Use a multiplier: 100% plus the increase, or 100% minus the decrease. Percentage change is always out of the original amount.

cards.title: Profits and discounts
cards.rule: Profit = selling price − cost price. Profit % is out of the cost price.

cards.title: Income
cards.rule: Wage: paid per hour. Salary: a set amount a year. Commission: a % of sales.
lines: $28/h: time and a half **$42/h**, double time **$56/h**

cards.title: The PAYG income tax system
cards.rule: Pay As You Go: your employer takes tax out of each pay and sends it to the ATO.

cards.title: Simple interest
cards.rule: The same interest every year, worked out on the amount you started with.
lines: \(I = Prt\): principal, rate as a decimal, time in years

cards.title: Compound interest and depreciation
cards.rule: Compound: interest is added each year, then earns interest too. Depreciation: value drops by a % each year.
lines: Depreciation \(A = P(1 - r)^n\): a $20 000 car losing 15% a year is worth \(20\,000 \times 0.85^2 = \$14\,450\) after 2 years
cards.note: Interest earned = A − P. Here $247.20, more than simple interest ($240).
